gaps.sentence: To such extremes ___ the fans go that the police were called in.
gaps.explanation: 'To such extremes did the fans go that …' — inverted past simple.

gaps.sentence: Only since the redesign ___ the app gained new users.
gaps.explanation: 'Only since the redesign has the app gained …' — perfect inversion.

gaps.sentence: Should the temperature ___ 40 degrees, the system shuts down.
gaps.explanation: Should the temperature exceed… = if it exceeds… — technical register.

gaps.sentence: At no point ___ the pilot leave the cockpit.
gaps.explanation: At no point did… = never did… — negative adverbial inversion.

gaps.sentence: Rarely ___ we seen such dedication from a new recruit.
gaps.explanation: 'Rarely have we seen' — inversion with present perfect, experience up to now.

gaps.sentence: Only when the results were published ___ the scale of the error become clear.
gaps.explanation: 'Only when … did the scale … become clear' — inverted past simple.

gaps.sentence: No sooner ___ the contract been signed than the rumours started.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner had … been signed than …' — past perfect with inversion.

gaps.sentence: ___ as it may sound, the machine still works perfectly.
gaps.explanation: Adjective + as + subject + verb = although it sounds strange.
